narrative: Demand for PL2__M4410282 is continuous with moderate variability (CV=0.39) and a detectable upward trend across the observation window, suggesting growing consumption. Lead times average 2.74 days with moderate variability after excluding four data-artifact near-zero observations; this is substantially shorter than the current SAP safety lead time of 5 days. The (r,Q) policy is selected as the material exhibits regular, positive demand with no intermittency, making a fixed reorder-point / fixed-order-quantity model both practical and cost-efficient. The storage cap of 566,887 units binds the order quantity at 511,833 units and is explicitly verified as feasible (SS + Q = 566,887 ≤ capacity).
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ of 625,570 units reduced to 511,833 units to satisfy max_storage_units=566,887.
4 near-zero lead time observations (<=0.1 days) excluded as data artifacts.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous (100% non-zero days), moderate CV of 0.39, and the material has a well-defined MOQ. The (r,Q) model is appropriate: trigger a fixed replenishment of Q=511,833 units whenever stock falls to the reorder point r=128,729 units, providing 95% cycle-service-level protection.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds EOQ: order quantity reduced from 625,570 to 511,833 units. This increases ordering frequency slightly (from 10.7 to 13.2 orders/year) and marginally reduces holding cost, but the net effect is still a 66.3% annual cost saving over SAP baseline. If storage is expanded in future, reverting to the unconstrained EOQ would yield further savings.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (96,491) + safety stock (55,054) = 151,545 which is well within max_storage_units (566,887). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
